passages.title: Sam's New Map
sentences: Sam got a new map of Harbor Town.
He put the map on his desk.
It showed the bus station and the ferry.
Sam found the skate park with his finger.
Then he found the library.
He put a red dot on his house.

passages.title: Priya's Rover
sentences: Priya built a small rover for robotics club.
She put the rover on the kitchen table.
Then she pressed a green button.
It rolled to the end of the table.
Priya caught it at the edge.
She smiled and turned the rover around.

passages.title: The Harbor Ferry
sentences: The Harbor Town ferry is big and white.
Every morning, it leaves the dock at 9 AM.
Cars drive onto the lower deck.
People sit on the top deck and look at the sea.
The trip to Gull Island takes one hour.
Then the ferry comes back to town.

passages.title: Leo's New Trick
sentences: On Saturday afternoon, Leo and Maya went to the skate park.
Leo wanted to show Maya a new trick.
He put his board at the top of the ramp.
Maya sat on a bench with her sketchbook.
She wanted to draw the trick.
Leo rolled down the ramp and jumped.
The board flipped under his feet.
He landed on it with both feet.
Maya clapped and cheered.
She held up her drawing of the jump.
Leo laughed and gave her a high five.

passages.title: Ben's Shiny Rock
sentences: Ben brought a shiny rock to science class.
He found it near the creek in Story Woods.
Ms. Ortiz looked at the rock with a magnifying glass.
She said it was a piece of quartz.
Ben asked if he could keep the rock.
Ms. Ortiz smiled and gave it back to him.
Then she showed the class her own rock collection.

rows: Hi Sam. Priya came to the bakery after school.
She left her rover on the counter.
Can you take it to her house tonight?
Pixel can go with you. He loves Priya!

passages.title: The Bus to the Observatory
sentences: Sam and Leo planned to take the nine o'clock bus to the observatory.
Sam got to the bus station twenty minutes early.
He held a map of Lantern Peaks and watched the door.
At 8:58, Leo ran in with his skateboard under one arm.
Sam waved at him and pointed to the bus.
Leo was breathing hard.
"A wheel came off my board on the way here," Leo said.
Sam smiled and handed him a ticket.
The bus driver checked the tickets, and the two boys found seats at the back.
Leo fixed the loose wheel with a small tool from his bag.
Sam traced the road up the hill on the map.
At ten o'clock, the bus stopped in front of the observatory.

passages.title: Muffins for the Team
sentences: Ana and Ben Diaz play on the Harbor Middle School soccer team.
On Friday morning, the twins stopped at Rose's Bakery before school.
They wanted to buy a snack for the team.
Grandma Rose had a tray of fresh banana muffins.
Sam was at the counter, helping his grandma.
The twins counted their money.
They had twelve dollars, so they asked for twelve muffins.
Sam put the muffins in a big box and closed the lid.
Then he carried it out to the bus stop for them.
At lunch, the whole team shared the muffins.

passages.title: Sea Glass
sentences: On Sunday, Maya and Priya walked along the beach near the harbor.
Maya was looking for sea glass, which is old glass that the ocean has made smooth.
Priya was testing a metal detector that she had built in robotics club.
After an hour, Maya found three pieces of green glass in the wet sand.
They were cloudy and round, because the waves had rubbed them for years.
Then Priya's detector beeped next to a log, and she dug up an old brass key.
Maya held the key up to the light and drew it in her sketchbook.
Then she gave it back to Priya, who put it in her pocket.

passages.title: The Old Bikes
sentences: Mr. Okafor had two old bikes in the back of his shop, and nobody had ridden them for years.
Their tires were flat, and their chains were brown with rust.
On Saturday morning, Ben asked if he could fix them for the school bike club.
Mr. Okafor agreed, but he said that Ben needed a helper for a job this big.
Ben called Sam, who arrived twenty minutes later with Pixel on a leash.
Mr. Okafor showed the boys how to take off a chain and soak it in a tray of cleaner.
While the chains soaked, Sam pumped air into the tires.
He found a tiny hole in one of them, so he fixed it with a patch from a kit on the shelf.
His careful work surprised Ben.
When Ben asked about it, Sam explained that his grandma had taught him on her old delivery bike.
By closing time, both bikes were clean, oiled and ready to ride.
Mr. Okafor told the boys that they could ride them to school on Monday to show the bike club.

passages.title: The Comic Club
sentences: In September, Maya and Ana started a comic club at the Harbor Town library.
Every Thursday after school, six students met at a long table by the window.
They each drew one page, and at the end of every month, they joined the pages into one long comic.
In October, the club invented a story about a robot that lives inside the old lighthouse.
The robot never goes outside without its tiny yellow umbrella.
Maya drew the robot with copper arms and a round glass head.
Ana wrote the words in the speech bubbles, because she is the best at jokes.
The librarian, Mrs. Hall, liked the finished comic so much that she asked if she could put it in the glass case by the front door.
The club voted yes.
Now people stop to read it while they wait to borrow their books.

passages.title: The Robotics Fair
sentences: The island robotics fair took place in the gym at Harbor Middle School on the first Saturday in November.
Teams from four schools brought machines that they had designed, built and programmed themselves.
Some of them could climb small staircases, and others could sort objects by color and size.
Priya had built a rover that could pick up colored blocks with a claw, and Maya had designed a painted shell to cover its wires.
The two girls had worked on it together for six weeks.
An hour before the judging began, Priya noticed that the claw would not close all the way.
She examined the motor while Maya held a flashlight, and together the girls discovered a loose screw.
Their tiny screwdriver was still in Ms. Ortiz's bag, and their teacher was at the other end of the gym.
Maya hurried across the gym to find her, and she came back two minutes later with the screwdriver and their teacher.
Ms. Ortiz did not repair the claw herself.
Instead, she handed the screwdriver to Priya and told her that there was still enough time.
Priya tightened the screw with steady hands, and the claw closed with a soft, satisfying click.
When the judges reached the table, they asked the girls to show what the rover could do.
Priya steered it toward a pile of blocks, and it picked up the red ones first, then the blue ones.
One judge asked who had painted the shell, and Priya pointed to Maya.
Later that afternoon, the girls won a blue ribbon for the most creative design.
On Monday, they hung it above the workbench in Ms. Ortiz's room.

passages.title: The Gull on the Rail
sentences: Leo and Maya ate lunch on a bench by the harbor.
A big white and gray gull landed on the rail next to them.
It looked at Leo's sandwich and tipped its head.
Leo held his sandwich close to his chest.
Maya opened her sketchbook and began to draw the gull.
She drew its yellow beak and its pink feet.
Then a boat horn blew, and the gull flew away over the water.
Leo laughed and finished his lunch.
Maya showed him her drawing.

passages.title: The Bridge Game
sentences: On Saturday, the library held a video game contest for teams of three.
Ana, Ben and Leo called their team the Lighthouse Crew.
In the game, they had to build a bridge before the timer ran out.
Ben steered a truck that carried logs to the river.
Leo placed each log on the bridge and checked that the logs were straight.
Ana watched the timer and called out the seconds.
With ten seconds left, the truck got stuck in the mud.
Leo told Ben to back up and try the other road.
He turned the truck around, and it rolled onto the bridge just in time.
The other teams clapped when the bridge was finished.
The Lighthouse Crew won second place, and each player got a small trophy.

passages.title: The Hard Part
sentences: Maya plays the flute and Priya plays the cello in the school band.
On Tuesday, Ms. Gray gave the band a new song with a hard part in the middle.
Maya could play the fast notes, but she kept losing her place in the music.
Priya could keep her place, but her fingers were too slow for the fast notes.
So the two girls made a plan.
After school, Maya played the hard part slowly, again and again.
Priya played along with her and counted the beats out loud.
Then Priya pointed to each note while Maya played it.
By Friday, she could play the fast part without losing her place, and Priya's fingers were faster too.
Ms. Gray asked the girls to play the hard part together for the band.
When they finished, the whole band clapped.

passages.title: Pixel's Find
sentences: In late August, after a long, dry summer, the creek in Story Woods was lower than Sam had ever seen it.
Sam walked along the dry edge with Pixel, who sniffed every rock and stick.
Near a bend, Pixel stopped beside a flat gray rock and sniffed at it.
Then he began to dig at a hollow in the rock that was full of dried mud.
Sam knelt down and brushed the mud away with his fingers.
Under it was a shape with three long toes, as wide as a dinner plate.
Sam took a photo with his phone and sent it to Ms. Ortiz.
She came to the creek that afternoon and studied the shape for a long time.
Then she told Sam that it might be a dinosaur footprint.
She called the Harbor Town Museum, and two scientists came the next morning.
They measured the print, took photos from every side and made a plaster copy of it.
A week later, Dr. Bell, one of the scientists, phoned Ms. Ortiz with news.
She said that the footprint was real and that it was more than 66 million years old.
The museum would keep the plaster copy, but the real print would stay in the creek where Pixel had found it.
Beside the copy, the museum put a small sign: "Found by Sam Rivera and his dog, Pixel."

passages.title: Storm on the Bay
sentences: Captain Ruth Lane has steered the Harbor Town ferry for twenty years.
On Wednesday afternoon, she was getting ready to sail from Gull Island back to town.
Her deckhand, Kim Torres, was checking the ropes and the life jackets.
Before they left, the captain looked at the weather radar on her screen.
A storm was moving across the bay, and it was heading toward the island fast.
Its winds were strong enough to push tall waves against the side of the ferry.
Captain Lane decided that the ferry would stay at the Gull Island dock until the storm had passed.
She asked Kim to tie it to the dock with two extra ropes.
Kim pulled each knot tight, and then she checked them twice.
Inside, forty passengers were waiting on the benches.
The captain told them about the storm and the new plan.
Some of them were disappointed, but they understood.
For an hour, heavy rain hit the windows, and the ferry rocked gently at the dock.
Kim handed out cups of hot cocoa from the snack counter, and the passengers played cards or read.
Then the clouds moved east, and the radar showed that the storm had passed.
The captain started the engines, and the ferry left the island with all of its passengers.
It reached Harbor Town at six o'clock, one hour late.

passages.title: The Xylophone Robot
sentences: For the spring music night, Ms. Gray asked every club at Harbor Middle School to add something to the show.
The robotics club decided to build a robot that could play a song on a xylophone.
A xylophone is an instrument with a row of wooden bars, and each bar makes a different note when it is struck.
Priya designed the robot, and Ana wrote the program that told it which bars to hit.
The robot had two thin arms, and each arm held a mallet with a hard rubber tip.
At first, the mallets pressed against the bars after each hit, so they made dull thuds instead of clear notes.
Priya added a small spring behind each mallet, and after that they bounced off the bars right away, the way a player's mallets do.
Ana slowed the song down, because the robot's arms could not move as quickly as a person's.
By the end of the week, it could play the whole song without a single wrong note.
On music night, Priya carried the robot onto the stage and set it in front of the xylophone.
Then she realized that this xylophone was longer than the one at school, so its bars were in different places.
Ana opened her laptop and changed the distances in the program while Priya measured the bars with a ruler.
The two girls finished in eight minutes, and the audience waited quietly.
When Ms. Gray gave the signal, the robot lifted its arms and began to play.
Its mallets bounced from bar to bar, and everyone in the gym could hear the clear notes of the song.
At the end, the audience clapped for a long time, and some people came to the stage to take photos of it.
Priya smiled at Ana, and Ana gave her a quick thumbs-up.

passages.title: The Beaver Pond
sentences: A family of beavers lives on the creek above the old mill in Story Woods.
Beavers are large rodents, the same group of animals as mice and squirrels, and they spend much of their lives in and around water.
A beaver can stay underwater for up to fifteen minutes, and it uses its flat tail to steer when it swims.
The beavers built a dam across the creek from sticks, mud and stones.
It blocks the moving water, so a wide, still pond has formed behind it.
To get wood, beavers cut down small trees with their sharp front teeth.
Their teeth keep growing for their whole lives, but chewing wood wears them down, so they never get too long.
Most of this work happens at night, when the beavers are busiest.
In the middle of the pond, the family lives in a lodge, a round home made of sticks packed with mud.
Its doors are underwater, so other animals cannot easily get inside.
In autumn, the beavers push branches into the mud at the bottom of the pond.
In winter, when ice covers the pond, they swim out under the ice and eat the bark from them.
The pond is important to many other animals as well.
Ducks and frogs raise their young in it, and fish hide among its plants.
When scientists study beaver ponds, they often find more kinds of animals there than along the rest of the creek.

items.explain: "It" means the ferry. The sentence before says the ferry would stay at the dock, so Kim tied the ferry to the dock.

items.prompt: The second paragraph starts: "Its winds were strong enough to push tall waves against the side of the ferry." What does "Its" mean?
items.hint: This paragraph starts with a pronoun. Read the last sentence of the paragraph before. Ask which thing has winds.
items.explain: "Its" means the storm's. The last sentence of the first paragraph is about the storm, and a storm has strong winds.

items.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with names or things. Choose what "she" and "them" mean.
items.frame: Kim pulled each knot tight, and then {0} checked {1} twice.
items.hint: Find who was pulling the knots at the start of the same sentence. Then ask what she would check after she tied them.
items.explain: Kim pulled each knot tight, and then Kim checked the knots twice. "She" and "them" point back to the start of the same sentence, in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Read: "Some of them were disappointed, but they understood." Who are "they"?
options: the passengers waiting on the benches
the people waiting in Harbor Town
items.hint: "They" means more than one person. Read the two sentences before. Ask who heard about the new plan.
items.explain: "They" means the passengers. The captain told the passengers about the plan, and some of them were disappointed, but they understood. It is at the end of the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Read: "Priya added a small spring behind each mallet, and after that they bounced off the bars right away, the way a player's mallets do." What does "they" mean?
items.hint: Several things in this sentence are more than one. Ask which ones hit the bars and could bounce off them.
items.explain: "They" means the robot's mallets. The mallets hit the bars, and after Priya added the springs, the mallets bounced off. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Read: "By the end of the week, it could play the whole song without a single wrong note." What does "it" mean?
items.hint: "It" means one thing. Ask which thing in the story plays the song on the xylophone.
items.explain: "It" means the robot. The robot plays the xylophone, and by the end of the week, the robot could play the whole song. It is the last sentence of the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Rewrite the sentence. Choose who "she" means and whose bars "its" means.
items.frame: Then {0} realized that this xylophone was longer than the one at school, so {1} bars were in different places.
items.hint: Read the sentence before to find who carried the robot to the xylophone. Then ask which xylophone had bars in new places.
items.explain: Priya realized that this xylophone was longer than the one at school, so this xylophone's bars were in different places. Priya is named in the sentence before, at the start of the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Read: "Their teeth keep growing for their whole lives, but chewing wood wears them down, so they never get too long." What does "they" mean?
items.hint: Ask what could get too long. Then look for it earlier in the same sentence.
items.explain: "They" means the beavers' teeth. The teeth keep growing, chewing wears them down, so the teeth never get too long. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Read: "It blocks the moving water, so a wide, still pond has formed behind it." What does "It" mean?
items.hint: "It" means one thing. Read the sentence before. Ask which thing could block moving water.
items.explain: "It" means the dam. The sentence before says the beavers built a dam across the creek, and the dam blocks the water. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Read: "In winter, when ice covers the pond, they swim out under the ice and eat the bark from them." What does "them" mean?
options: the small trees on the bank
items.hint: "They" and "them" mean different things here. "They" are the swimmers. Read the sentence before to find what has bark and is under the ice.
items.explain: "Them" means the branches. In autumn, the beavers push branches into the mud, and in winter they eat the bark from the branches. It is at the end of the third paragraph.

steps.say: I see the word 'She'. 'She' means a girl or a woman.
I look back for a name that comes before it.
The first sentence names Priya. Priya is the only person in this story.
